articles.title: Femtosecond Laser Welding of N-BK7 Glass: From In-Volume Modification to Large-Scale, High-Strength Joining
articles.authors: Manon Lafargue, Théo Guilberteau, Michael Jarwitz, Bastien Gavory, John Lopez, Inka Manek-Hönninger
articles.summary: Femtosecond laser welding enables the direct joining of transparent materials through localized energy deposition and melting at the interface. However, achieving high joint strength and welding over large areas remain challenging due to high thermal gradients generated during processing, which can lead to crack appearance. In this study, N-BK7 glass was irradiated using a femtosecond laser source emitting 500 fs pulses at 1030 nm to investigate the influence of energy deposition and temporal pulse distribution on laser-induced modifications. Repetitive single-pulse irradiation was compared to burst modes operating at 40 MHz and 1.28 GHz. …

articles.title: Parallel DNA AND Logic Processing with Threshold-Gated Whispering-Gallery-Mode Microcavity Laser Arrays
articles.authors: Chan Seok Jun, Wonsuk Lee
articles.summary: DNA strand-displacement logic circuits can recognize combinations of nucleic-acid inputs, whereas optical microcavity lasers provide a nonlinear threshold that converts molecular events into binary optical signals. Here, we demonstrate a parallel DNA logic-processing platform in which three independent two-input AND gates are coupled to spatially separated whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) microcavity laser readouts in a three-channel PDMS microfluidic device. Each channel implements a distinct pair of DNA inputs and generates an output strand only when both cognate targets are present; the output is expected to increase the amount of cavity-associated SYTO dye and thereby the optical gain. …

articles.title: Synthesis of Fe2O3–Au Nanostructures by Pulsed Laser Ablation in Liquids: Systematic Study of the Effects of Liquid Medium and Ablation Parameters
articles.authors: Elder Alejandro Meza Ramírez, Armando Pérez Centeno, Enrique Campos-González, Enrique Camps, José Guadalupe Quiñones Galván
articles.summary: Au-Fe2O3 heterostructure nanoparticles were synthesized via liquid-phase laser ablation to study how different routes affect their morphology and plasmonic response, specifically comparing two reversed target-colloid configurations, a parameter scarcely explored in these hybrid systems. Eight samples were prepared using two colloid/target configurations: ablation of a metallic gold target in Fe2O3 nanoparticle colloid or ablation of a Fe2O3 target in a preformed Au nanoparticles colloid. Water and acetone medium were used, with laser fluences of 0.23 and 0.39 J cm−2, and ablation times of 4 and 10 min under 532 nm irradiation. …

articles.title: Ultrafast Laser Synthesis of Titanium Silicalite-1 Zeolite: Titanium Substitution Behavior
articles.authors: Hagverdiyev M, Doğan MM, Miura A, Doi S, Kaya M, Galioglu S
articles.summary: Controlling heteroatom substitution while suppressing undesired secondary phases remains a fundamental challenge in zeolite synthesis. Here we show that ultrafast laser driven far-from-equilibrium microreactors provide a fundamentally different pathway for heteroatom substitution compared to conventional near equilibrium hydrothermal synthesis. Titanium Silicalite-1 (TS-1) zeolite is a model system to investigate volume upgrade potential of the ultrafast laser synthesis method because titanium substitution is highly sensitive to synthesis dynamics. …

articles.title: Depth-robust super-resolution nanofabrication for 3D mesoscopic photonic structures
articles.authors: Li Z, Wang Y, Shao C, Xu J, Dong D, Zhou S, Huang X, Yang H, Sun Y, Shi K
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Molecular Oncology
articles.summary: Mesoscopic optical systems underpin photonic interconnects, on-chip metrology, quantum computing and miniature microscopy, but monolithic integration of these components is currently limited by fabrication methodologies that only offer limited depth control. At depth, the super-resolution performance of stimulated-emission-depletion direct laser writing is hindered by absorption, scattering and aberrations arising from refractive index mismatch that distort the depletion focus. Here we show that maintaining axial alignment between the excitation and depletion fields overcomes this limitation. …

articles.title: Femtosecond laser-controlled production of functional titanium niobate layers from TiO2/Nb2O5 powders
articles.authors: Gonzalo Gomez-Munoz, Aarón Calvo-Villoslada, Inmaculada Álvarez-Serrano, María Luisa López, Paloma Fernández, Javier Solis, Belén Sotillo
articles.summary: Conventional synthesis methods of titanium niobates (TNO) require prolongated high-temperature treatments. To overcome this limitation, in this work, we have developed a confined powder-bed femtosecond (fs) laser-based technique to sinter TNO films starting from a mixture of TiO2 and Nb2O5 powders, avoiding furnace-based approaches. The influence of laser-processing conditions on film formation, phase composition, and microstructure is systematically investigated, demonstrating that different TNO phases and morphologies can be obtained by controlling the laser pulse energy. …

articles.title: Quantitative evaluation of single-grating phase-contrast imaging with a femtosecond laser–plasma Kα X-ray source
articles.authors: Georges Giakoumakis, Amelie Ferré, Daria Gudz, Mouad Saliji, Jérôme Primot, Olivier Utéza, Raphaël Clady, Adrien Stolidi
articles.summary: We present the first implementation of an X-ray phase-contrast imaging approach using single 2D-grating phase retrieval and a quasi-monochromatic hard K α X-ray source generated via high-intensity femtosecond laser—plasma interaction. To highlight its pertinence, we demonstrate quantitative phase-contrast measurements of a known canonical physical object, retrieving phase distribution with high-fidelity, under varying experimental conditions. As a marker of such performance, a correlation score of up to 0.922 ± 0.008 is obtained between theoretical and experimental phase images. …

articles.title: A novel optical scanning system for laser machining of vertical sidewall
articles.authors: Jaehee Kim, Dongsik Kim, Hyun Choi, Jeonghong Ha
institutions: Pohang University of Science and Technology
articles.summary: Despite its many advantages, laser micromachining has limitations, such as tapering due to plasma-induced distortion, gaussian beam profiles, and defocusing effects. Although process parameter optimization and adjusting the angle-of-incidence (AOI) have been investigated to reduce tape angle of the sidewall, existing approaches often require complex process optimization, workpiece tilting, or multi-axis scanning systems. In this study, we developed a novel optical scanning system consisting of three spherical lenses and a 2D galvanometer scanner to enable AOI variation using a simplified optical configuration. …

articles.title: Galvanometer Mirror Based Femtosecond-Laser Volumetric Displays
articles.authors: Katsuhito Muroi, Ryosei Kojima, Tatsuki Fushimi, Yoichi Ochiai
articles.summary: Femtosecond-laser-induced plasma enables self-emissive voxels to be generated directly in air for drawing three-dimensional images. Galvanometer-mirror-based beam scanning provides a method for rapidly moving plasma voxels using a relatively simple optical configuration. However, the generated plasma voxels are not ideal points but luminous regions with finite lengths and widths. Variations in voxel shape and orientation caused by focusing and scanning conditions may therefore affect the appearance of rendered points and lines. …
